prerequisites: Engineering Mathematics I and II, especially differential equations

learning_outcomes.text: Students know and can state the fundamental heat transfer and heat exchanger mechanisms, the physical-mathematical backgrounds, balances, and relationships describing them.
Students know relevant dimensionless characteristic numbers and can use them to characterize heat transfer problems.
They understand how to analyze complex heat transfer processes and make appropriate estimations to apply simplifying solution approaches and methods.
Students can independently critically analyze, estimate, and arrive at critically reflected results for complex problems.
Homework and exercise assignments with submission deadlines can be solved independently or in self-organized small groups. A qualified exchange with other students is possible.

bibliography: Howell, John R./Mengüc, M. Pinar/Siegel, Robert: Thermal Radiation Heat Transfer, CRC Press: Boca Raton/London/New York (6. Auflage) 2006.
